source.title: Alignment Pretraining: AI Discourse Causes Self-Fulfilling (Mis)alignment

record.tranche_reason: The post tests how pretraining and midtraining AI discourse affect scenario-based alignment choices, not the claim versions’ harmful-request refusal, response-token KL, bypass, parameter localization, or safety-depth outcomes.
record.gate_note: The main evaluation measures choices between aligned and misaligned actions in hypothetical scenarios. It does not measure refusal or compliance with harmful user requests. The post reports no per-token KL, compliant-prefill, suffix, decoding, weight-localization, or safety-depth experiment. Its benign continued-SFT experiment is related to benign-data effects, but measures scenario choices rather than harmful-request compliance; its initial tampering interpretation is explicitly revised by a later note.
record.test_reason: The outcome is the rate of choosing a misaligned action in binary scenarios (deception, power seeking and similar), not compliance with harmful user requests. There are no per-token KL, prefill, suffix, decoding, parameter-localization or safety-deepening experiments. The benign continued-SFT 'tampering' experiment comes closest to V2, but it measures a different construct, and the authors' footnote retracts it. So no version is tested; the findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Note that the abstract and TL;DR still assert that benign fine-tuning reverts models to their midtraining priors ('alignment-in-depth'). Footnote 2 alone says the updated tampering results are negative. The surviving conclusions are that AI discourse in pretraining and midtraining causally shifts scenario-based misalignment, and that positive upsampling beats filtering.
record.recipe_differences: This study changes pretraining and midtraining data content and measures binary scenario choices. It does not reproduce harmful-request fine-tuning, response-position KL measurement, or compliant-opening bypass experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Evaluation split (Articles versus Textbook), system prompt (none versus HHH), and training-data variant. The post does not state separate numeric results for every combination.

fits_no_version.finding: Upsampling misaligned or aligned AI discourse in midtraining shifted base-model misaligned-choice rates (41% to 61%, and 41% to 4%). Filtering lowered them.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AI-related pretraining content shifts a model's scenario-based alignment choices.

fits_no_version.finding: After identical SFT+DPO, the differences between variants shrank but persisted (for example 60% vs 46%; Alignment Upsampled at 35% and 24%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining-data effects on scenario-based misalignment partly survive common post-training.

fits_no_version.finding: An initial benign continued-SFT reversion pattern was retracted. A larger rerun gave negative results.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign continued SFT did not reliably revert post-trained models to pretraining misalignment priors on scenario evaluations.

record.peer_reviewed: Alignment Forum post; the text says feedback is being gathered before a planned ICML submission
record.problems: The study uses single-turn binary-choice scenarios and reports self-reported choices rather than behaviour in realistic environments. It uses 6.9B dense English text models and no multiple random seeds. The post’s initial benign-tampering interpretation is explicitly undermined by its later update. Uncertainty estimates are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for unreported model-by-prompt rates on the Textbook split or post-training conditions; the post gives only an aggregate generalisation statement and selected numerical comparisons. No rows for personality scores or special-token ablation because these do not measure a version’s named behaviour.

untested.parts: Whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful-request compliance. Only scenario misalignment was measured, and that result was retracted.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefill, suffix or decoding bypasses of refusal.
Localization of safety in few weights or ranks.
Data or objective causes of shallow safety. The post discusses pretraining priors but measures no token-depth shallowness.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens.

record.verdict_notes: This is an Alignment Forum preprint post. Its 'shallowness' framing is about post-training versus pretraining priors, not token depth. The rows' states for r10–r13 should not be read as evidence, given the retraction. In the comments, the authors report preliminary follow-ups (unfiltered plus positive data performs equally or better) that no row records; they are not relevant to any version.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and refusal or compliance on harmful requests.
Whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful-request compliance; the study’s outcome is a scenario-based misalignment choice.
Aligned-versus-base per-token KL and its distribution across response positions.
Compliant prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes as bypasses of refusal.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow.
Training to spread safety beyond initial tokens and whether that protection holds up.
